headline: Brooklyn’s Nostrand Houses secures $607M modernization deal
dek: The first project financed through New York City’s Public Housing Preservation Trust will renovate 1,148 apartments while keeping the Sheepshead Bay development public and permanently affordable.
body: A $607 million financing closing will fund a full modernization of Nostrand Houses in Sheepshead Bay, Brooklyn, New York City officials announced Wednesday. The project will rehabilitate 1,148 apartments in 16 residential buildings serving about 2,000 residents, making it the first development to reach financial closing through the New York City Public Housing Preservation Trust.

The investment is aimed at the kind of accumulated work that is difficult to address through isolated repairs. The Mayor’s Office said every kitchen and bathroom will be renovated, while building-wide work will cover heating, domestic hot water, electrical wiring, plumbing and elevators. Apartments are also slated for new appliances, energy-efficient windows, intercom systems and resident-controlled heating and cooling. Lead and mold hazards will be remediated as part of the renovation, according to the city’s announcement.

The financing matters beyond one Brooklyn development because it tests whether the Trust can help New York City move more public housing from deferred maintenance toward comprehensive rehabilitation. Nostrand Houses will remain 100 percent public, continue to be managed by the New York City Housing Authority and keep permanently affordable rents and resident protections. The Trust structure converts the property to project-based Section 8 and, paired with a long-term ground lease, allows the development to access a federal operating subsidy that the city says will be roughly twice what it currently receives.

Residents helped determine whether that structure would apply to their homes. Nostrand Houses residents voted in December 2023 to become the first NYCHA development to join the Trust. Since then, the modernization plan has been shaped through surveys, design workshops, community meetings, a model apartment review and a Construction Council. The city says residents selected interior design packages and helped set priorities for the work, including the logistics of temporary relocations.

The planned upgrades include 81 apartments adapted for residents with mobility needs and 48 apartments adapted for residents with visual or hearing impairments. Security work will add access-control improvements and expanded camera coverage. NYCHA plans to operate a new on-site management office with more than 40 staff members, while Kings Bay Y will provide case management, housing-stability assistance, crisis intervention and programs for health, youth, families, seniors and workforce development.

The project also includes a smaller wealth-building component for children who live at Nostrand Houses. The Trust said it will contribute $100 each year through high school graduation to NYC Scholarship Accounts for eligible children, in partnership with NYC Kids RISE. That program does not replace the housing work, but it links the renovation to a broader effort to keep residents in permanently affordable homes while building educational and financial opportunities for the next generation.

Construction is expected to begin in fall 2026, with the Trust’s project page identifying a phased process and an estimated completion in winter or spring 2031. The page also says the first phase of resident relocations is expected to start in October. For residents, the immediate question will be how the work is sequenced and how support is provided during moves; for the city, the longer test will be whether Nostrand becomes a workable model for other NYCHA developments that choose to pursue the Trust. The project details and timeline are posted by the Public Housing Preservation Trust at https://www.preservationtrust.org/trustmodprogram/nostrand.
location: Nostrand Houses, Sheepshead Bay, Brooklyn, New York
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoDescription: A $607 million financing closing will modernize 1,148 apartments at Nostrand Houses while preserving public ownership and permanent affordability.
